title: Migrate @earendil-works/chord -> @oh-my-pi/chord by verbatim copy + scope/extension/vitest/format rewrite; FIRST of the 7 new packages, and the only one with an external npm dep (esbuild)
one_line: Chord is the application-composition runtime the other six new packages sit on top of: 30 source files / 314681 bytes implementing facet lifecycle (activate/dispose with reverse-order effect drain and error isolation), an immutable delta/CRDT engine (tracker 2205 lines, diff, apply, encoder/decoder, prototype-pollution guards), a Context cancellation scope, and a remote-service provider/consumer/instance-directory layer. omp has NONE of it — a 0-hit sweep for all 30 load-bearing symbol names across packages/**/*.ts. The migration is ~95% mechanical: 25 scope strings, 84 `.ts` import suffixes, 19 vitest imports, a 4-space-to-tab reformat, 3 forbidden `ReturnType<>` and 1 forbidden `new Promise`. The one real risk is a live semantic disagreement about what a teardown drain should do on error (see collisions #1).
why_copy_not_reimplement:
Four concrete reasons, each tied to a contract a rewrite would silently lose.

(1) The delta engine is a proven CRDT with a non-obvious correctness argument. src/delta/tracker.ts is 2205 lines / 78059 bytes and src/delta/index.ts another 694 — together 42% of the package. It maintains revision identity, structural sharing, and revision-vector-based causal ordering, and it defends against prototype pollution via a hard-coded RESERVED_SEGMENTS set ({__proto__, constructor, prototype}) at src/delta/index.ts:131 plus UnsafePathError (:133) and PathError (:310). Reimplementing that from a spec is how you ship a `__proto__` write-through bug. Copying it means the guard set and its tests arrive together, already 56112 bytes of regression coverage in test/delta-tracker/tracker.test.ts (75 describe/it blocks).

(2) The facet teardown contract is subtle and already expressed in tests. src/facets/host.ts:125-142 is 18 lines that do four non-obvious things at once: drain effects in REVERSE registration order (`.splice(0).reverse()`), isolate each effect's failure in its own try/catch, clear observations/activate callbacks and flip #serviceAccess BEFORE surfacing, and aggregate (single error rethrown bare, multiple wrapped in AggregateError). test/facets.test.ts (20955 bytes) and test/facet-loader.test.ts (11801 bytes) assert the state machine transitions. Note this is the exact code M1 W2 was supposed to cite and could not — see collisions #1.

(3) The wire parsers are a hostile-input boundary. src/services/wire.ts exports 11 parse/create functions that all take `unknown` and return a narrowed type. These are the functions pi-server and pi-client call on bytes arriving off a socket. Their rejection behaviour (what happens to a malformed frame) is the contract, and it is only expressed as tests. Any rewrite re-derives the accept/reject boundary and gets a different one.

(4) The bundler is a whole subsystem with no test-free path. src/node/{bundle,bundle-loader,package}.ts (34677 bytes) drive esbuild, resolve `@earendil-works/chord` specifiers back to `../index.<ext>`, do SHA-256 subresource-integrity stamping, and write a content-addressed CommonJS manifest. src/services/state-codec.ts additionally turns service state into delta Ops on the wire — the bridge between the two halves of the package. Reimplementing that is ~3 days of work with no contract to test against except the 28 test files that would then have to be rewritten too.

new_dependencies.name: esbuild
new_dependencies.why: The ONLY external runtime dep of the entire package. Imported in exactly one file: src/node/bundle.ts:4 `import { type BuildOptions, build, type Message } from "esbuild"`. Every other external import in src/ is a node: builtin (node:crypto, node:fs/promises, node:module, node:os, node:path, node:url, node:vm). Confirmed absent from omp: no `"esbuild"` in the root package.json or any packages/*/package.json, and `ls -d node_modules/esbuild` returns No such file or directory. The only trace in bun.lock is line 1455, where esbuild appears as vite's OPTIONAL PEER (`peerDependencies: {..., "esbuild": "^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0", ...}`, `optionalPeers: [..., "esbuild", ...]`) — declared, never installed. 0.28.2 satisfies that range, so adding it creates no version conflict with vite.

collisions.what: Disposer teardown drain — SEMANTIC CONFLICT, and the M1 W2 premise is false. The task note says M1 W1/W2 'already manually ported reverse-order drain + error isolation from packages/chord/src/facets/host.ts:125-142'. Verified false in two ways. (1) The W2 spec's own plan_corrections record the claim as verdict 'unverifiable — the reference does not exist in this repo', evidence '`ls -d pi-ref` → No such file or directory; `find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -name host.ts -path \'*chord*\' -print` returns nothing', and the correction is 'Do not attempt to read chord.' (2) Nothing landed: `drainDisposers` does not exist anywhere in omp. The four drain loops W2 targeted are still the original forward-order, no-try/catch shape.
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:4983, packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:5218, packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/extension-ui-controller.ts:112, packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1347 — all four are `for (const dispose of this.#X.splice(0)) dispose();`
collisions.resolution: KEEP OMP. Copying chord must NOT mean converting these four loops. The two designs disagree on purpose: chord's FacetKernel.dispose drains reverse, isolates each error, then RETHROWS (`if (errors.length === 1) throw errors[0]; if (errors.length > 1) throw new AggregateError(errors, ...)`). W2's contract is to log and continue, because beginDispose() is called from session-teardown.ts:70 BEFORE the try that wraps `await deps.saveDraft(draftText)` — a throwing drain would reject teardown before the draft is written, turning a conditional leak into an unconditional data-loss path. That divergence is correct for omp. Re-implement the four loops against chord's FacetKernel as a SEPARATE, LATER change under W2's own spec, and when that happens keep log-and-continue. This spec only lands packages/chord; it changes zero lines in packages/coding-agent.

collisions.what: JsonValue — six definitions in omp, three distinct shapes. Highest-reach collision in the package because pi-server, pi-client, pi-durable, and pi-protocol all import chord's JsonValue.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/chord/src/types.ts:21 — `null | boolean | number | string | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue }`
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/catalog/src/discovery/protobuf.ts:11 (identical shape), packages/mnemopi/src/types.ts:2 (via JsonScalar, identical shape), packages/mnemopi/src/mcp-tools.ts:9 (via JsonPrimitive, identical shape), packages/mnemopi/src/core/beam/types.ts:4 (identical shape), packages/ai/src/judgment/types.ts:17 (READONLY variant: `readonly JsonValue[]` / `{ readonly [key: string]: JsonValue }`), packages/coding-agent/src/secrets/obfuscator.ts:72 (DIVERGENT: object branch is `{ [key: string]: JsonValue | undefined }`)
collisions.resolution: KEEP CHORD'S, but do NOT try to unify omp's six in this change. Copying chord's JsonValue verbatim is correct and non-breaking: all four sibling packages that import it were copied from the same pi tree and are mutually consistent. The obfuscator variant is a genuine divergence, but nothing in this migration passes an obfuscator value across the chord boundary, so unifying is out of scope. Record it as a follow-up: a single `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` JsonValue + isJsonValue, and have all six definitions plus chord's two import from there. Note pi-protocol's spec says it imports JsonValue and isJsonValue from chord — after this migration those come from @oh-my-pi/chord, and pi-protocol's copy must be pointed at that import rather than keeping its own.

collisions.what: Context — same name, entirely different concept.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/chord/src/types.ts:15 — immutable key/value cancellation scope: `value<T>(key: ContextKey<T>): T | undefined`, `toString()`, and an `abortSignal` getter
collisions.omp_anchor: packages/ai/src/types.ts:1476 — `export interface Context { systemPrompt?: string[]; messages: Message[]; tools?: Tool[]; inactiveTools?: Tool[] }`, a REQUEST PAYLOAD, exported from @oh-my-pi/pi-ai and imported by name in 10+ files
collisions.resolution: KEEP BOTH, DO NOT MERGE. They are unrelated and both are correct. The copy is safe today because no file star-imports both barrels — every one of the 10+ `@oh-my-pi/pi-ai` `Context` imports is a named import, and TS only reports an ambiguity on `export *` collisions. The residual risk is a future barrel re-export: if a module ever does `export * from "@oh-my-pi/pi-ai"` alongside `export * from "@oh-my-pi/chord"`, TS raises TS2308. Leave a comment at packages/chord/src/types.ts:15 naming pi-ai's unrelated Context so the next person does not try to unify them. Do not rename either symbol — durable, client, server, and protocol all import chord's Context by name and a rename would break four packages for no gain.

collisions.what: Draft — a much more permissive type in a codebase that forbids `any` elsewhere.
collisions.pi_anchor: packages/chord/src/delta/draft.ts:2 — recursive `-readonly` mapped type with an explicit depth cutoff at 8
collisions.omp_anchor: no Draft definition exists in omp at all (0 hits for `type Draft|interface Draft`)
collisions.resolution: NO COLLISION — but flag the intent. The cutoff exists so the compiler does not blow its stack on deep types. Keep it verbatim; do not 'simplify' it to an unbounded recursion. Zero `any` in chord's src (verified: `: any|<any>|as any|any[]` = 0), so copying does not import an `any` debt.

collisions.what: On-disk format strings that name the upstream package, which the package no longer is.
collisions.omp_anchor: no equivalent exists in omp; the bundler surface is entirely new
collisions.resolution: KEEP THE STRINGS VERBATIM. Do NOT rewrite them to "omp.…" as part of the scope rewrite. These are the identity of an on-disk artefact: a facet bundle written by pi must still load under @oh-my-pi/chord, and vice versa. Renaming them silently invalidates every bundle on disk. If omp ever wants its own format, that is a format-version bump, not a string edit in a migration commit.

test_contract:
22 test files, 28 blocks-groups, ~370 describe/it blocks, all rewritten vitest -> bun:test. Every one defends an observable contract; none is a static echo. The load-bearing groups, in priority order:

(1) test/delta-tracker/tracker.test.ts (56112 bytes, 75 blocks) — the CRDT. Causal ordering, revision identity, structural sharing, and what happens when two revisions of the same state are tracked concurrently. This is the file that makes the package worth copying rather than reimplementing.

(2) test/delta-apply-immutable.test.ts (9133 bytes, 9 blocks) — the SECURITY contract. Must prove that `apply`/`applyImmutable` on a path containing `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` THROWS UnsafePathError rather than writing through, and that the throwing is the observable result (not a silently skipped op). A regression that turns the throw into a no-op passes every other test in the package.

(3) test/facets.test.ts (20955 bytes, 15 blocks) + test/facet-loader.test.ts (11801 bytes, 10 blocks) — the lifecycle state machine. Must prove dispose() runs effects in REVERSE registration order, isolates a throwing effect so the remaining effects still run, and aggregates multiple failures. This is the anchor M1 W2 could not verify; after this migration the reference exists in-tree at packages/chord/src/facets/host.ts:125-142 and test/facets.test.ts is its executable documentation.

(4) test/service-wire.test.ts (9469 bytes, 8 blocks) — the hostile-input boundary. The 11 parsers in src/services/wire.ts take `unknown`; assert that each rejects malformed input with a specific outcome (undefined vs throw) and that a well-formed frame round-trips. This is a negative contract, which AGENTS.md explicitly endorses.

(5) test/bundle.test.ts (10829 bytes, 6 blocks) — proves the bundler still marks `@oh-my-pi/chord` external after the scope rewrite and that the manifest round-trips. This is the one file that cannot pass before `bun install` has actually fetched esbuild.

(6) test/boundary.test.ts (1504 bytes) — walks the package and asserts no upstream `@earendil-works/` specifier reaches a published entry. Not a banned source-grep: it is an import-resolution boundary check, not an assertion about code text.

(7) test/state-fuzz.test.ts (4282 bytes, 4 blocks) — fuzzing. Per AGENTS.md's termination exception, these must assert a BOUNDED output, a surfaced error, or a state change. A bare `not.toThrow()` is not acceptable and must be rejected in review.

Rules that apply to all 22: no `mock.module()` (Bun leaks the global module registry across files — oven-sh/bun#12823); no `vi.spyOn` on module namespaces that are imported as values; no source-grep assertions; no `expect(true).toBe(true)`; no length-grew or non-empty-string assertions without a consumer behind them; per-test cleanup with `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach` rather than file-wide mutation of Bun.*, process.env or process.platform. Anything copied from the source that does not meet these must be rewritten or deleted, not kept because it was green upstream.

risk:
MEDIUM, and the medium part is concentrated in one specific place.

The mechanical risk is low and self-announcing: a missed `.ts` suffix or a missed scope string is a compile error or a grep that does not return zero. `bun run check:ts` catches all of it.

The real risk is that copying chord's `dispose()` re-opens the M1 W2 drain question with the wrong answer. The task note says W1/W2 already manually ported the reverse-drain + error isolation and that copying 'wipes that risk clean' — that is half right and half wrong, and the half that is wrong is the dangerous half. Verified: (a) W2's own plan_corrections record the chord citation as 'unverifiable — the reference does not exist in this repo' with the correction 'Do not attempt to read chord', so no one ever read the source; (b) nothing landed — `drainDisposers` does not exist in omp and all four target loops still read `for (const dispose of this.#X.splice(0)) dispose();`, i.e. FORWARD order with no try/catch. So the four loops are currently neither W2's design nor chord's. Copying chord does not fix them, and it creates a new hazard: once packages/chord/src/facets/host.ts:125-142 exists in-tree with its `throw errors[0]` / `AggregateError` shape, the obvious-looking 'fix' is to route the four loops through it — and that would be a REGRESSION. W2 rejected that shape deliberately, because beginDispose() runs from session-teardown.ts:70 before the try that wraps `await deps.saveDraft(draftText)`, so a throwing drain converts a conditional resource leak into an unconditional draft-write failure. Mitigation: this change touches ZERO lines in packages/coding-agent, and step 15's `git diff --stat` check makes that verifiable.

Second-order risk: esbuild is a genuinely new runtime dependency in a repo that has been native-addon-only. It is MIT, it is a single well-known package, 0.28.2 satisfies vite's declared optional-peer range so nothing else moves, and it is imported by exactly one file — but it does mean `bun test packages/chord/test/bundle.test.ts` cannot pass until `bun install` has actually fetched it, and a fresh CI checkout that skips install will fail there rather than typecheck.

Third: the delta engine is 42% of the package and the reason to copy rather than rewrite, which also means the migration's value is entirely concentrated in whether those 75 tracker test blocks survive the vitest->bun:test conversion intact. If they get quietly trimmed to make the runner happy, the copy has lost its justification.
